utility.notes: Aurora, Illinois does not operate its own municipal electric utility (unlike neighboring Naperville) — its own 'Switch Together' solar group-buying program page does not name an alternate distribution utility, consistent with the well-documented fact that ComEd is the dominant investor-owned utility across Aurora's service area. Not independently cross-checked against a dedicated ComEd territory map this session.

value.name: Commonwealth Edison (ComEd)
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Aurora's residential solar customers this session; ComEd is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Aurora spans Kane, DuPage, Will, and Kendall counties; the city's own Building and Permits Division (not any one county) is the permitting authority regardless of which county a given parcel falls in.

permit_authority.value: City of Aurora Building and Permits Division
permit_authority.notes: Illinois has no single statewide residential solar permitting rule — permitting authority sits with the local municipality (inside its boundaries) or the county (in unincorporated areas).

permit_url.notes: The City's own Commercial/Residential Solar Application PDF and 2026 Fee Schedule PDF were both blocked this session — the fee schedule PDF returned HTTP 403 Forbidden via direct fetch and triggered a forced file-download prompt via the browser tool on separate attempts (the same genuine access-blocked pattern seen on other jurisdictions' fee documents this session), so their itemized contents could not be independently verified.

interconnection_url.notes: See the identical net-metering framework notes on the Chicago record (il-cook-chicago-comed) for ComEd's residential net-metering process and the caveat about the 2023-dated FAQ document relative to Illinois's reported 2025 Net Metering 2.0 policy change.

required_documents.notes: The application PDF itself was blocked this session (see permit_url notes), so its itemized document requirements beyond the form's existence could not be independently verified.

permit_fees.notes: The City's own 2026 Fee Schedule PDF was blocked this session (403 Forbidden via fetch; forced file-download via browser) — no fee figure was independently confirmed. A third-party estimate ('$127' for a commercial solar permit) appeared in search results but is not used since it is not confirmed as the residential figure nor independently verified against the City's own document.

value.name: Illinois Shines / Adjustable Block Program (ABP) — SREC incentive
value.description: The City of Aurora's own 'Solar In Aurora' page, describing its 2026 Switch Together group-buying program, states that 'Incentives through the Illinois Shines Program could provide 30% in savings for residents' — Illinois Shines is the public-facing brand for the Illinois Power Agency's statewide Adjustable Block Program (the SREC allocation mechanism also referenced on the Chicago record's ComEd source). The exact dollar/rate value was not independently confirmed from the Illinois Power Agency's own site this session.
value.eligibility: Illinois residential solar installations enrolled through an Illinois Shines-approved vendor; exact eligibility not independently confirmed this session.

rebates.notes: This is a statewide Illinois program (not Aurora-specific) referenced on Aurora's own page — the same underlying mechanism as the SREC/Adjustable Block Program reference on the Chicago record's ComEd source, now corroborated from a second, independent official source (a different Illinois municipality's own site).
